items.title: Having Multiple Partners Doesn't Hurt Sexual Health, Large Study Finds
items.summary: A study in the Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, led by Michelle Larva-Ruhala at the University of Turku, analyzed two large datasets and found that people in non-monogamous relationships (whether openly consensual or kept secret) reported sexual functioning, satisfaction, and health outcomes comparable to, and sometimes slightly better than, people in strictly monogamous relationships. Infidelity itself wasn't linked to worse sexual health, except that men who kept emotional or sexual intimacies secret from a partner reported lower satisfaction.
items.sowhat: It's a solid myth-buster against the idea that 'more partners' automatically means worse outcomes, which fits Nancy's no-judgment, your-relationship-your-rules messaging.
items.caption: New research files under 'things we already knew': however your relationship is structured, satisfaction comes down to honesty and communication, not a number. Secrecy's the only thing the data flagged as a problem 👀💛 However you're set up, keep talking to each other.

items.title: A Racing Heart From a Video Game Can Make Men Rate Dates as Hotter
items.summary: A study reported by PsyPost (posted as an SSRN preprint submitted to Computers in Human Behavior Reports) found that men who played a fast-paced, exciting virtual-reality game afterward rated online dating profiles as more attractive, an example of 'arousal misattribution,' where the brain reads leftover physical excitement from one source as romantic interest in another. The same carryover effect did not show up for women in the study.
items.sowhat: It's a fun, science-backed excuse for 'date night energy actually starts before the date,' and a reminder that excitement (a workout, a concert, a game night) can prime attraction.
items.caption: Plot twist from science: your heart rate doesn't know the difference between 'adrenaline' and 'attraction' 😅 So next date night, maybe start with something that gets the pulse up first. We won't say more. 💛

items.title: Study Links Autistic Traits to Fewer Affectionate 'Keep the Spark Alive' Habits
items.summary: A study in Evolutionary Psychology, led by Andrzej Lukasik at the University of Rzeszow, found that people in the general population with higher autistic-like traits were less likely to use affectionate, positive-maintenance behaviors (like small gestures of warmth) to sustain their romantic relationships. The researchers linked this mainly to attachment style rather than any broad evolutionary strategy, suggesting it's about how secure someone feels, not how much they care.
items.sowhat: A good reminder for Nancy's audience that affection styles differ person to person, and that small, intentional gestures of closeness are a learnable habit worth normalizing, not a universal default.
items.caption: Not everyone shows love the same way, and that's not a red flag, it's just a different love language. New research says affectionate habits are shaped more by how secure we feel than by how much we care. Translation: keep showing up for each other, your way. 💛

items.title: UK Criminalises Extreme Porn Categories, Tightens Platform Duties
items.summary: The UK government confirmed on October 16, 2026 that from November 6, three categories of explicit pornography — depicting strangulation/suffocation, pretend incest, and performers made to look under 16 — become criminal offences in England and Wales under the new Crime and Policing Act 2026. These categories are also designated 'priority offences' under the UK Online Safety Act, meaning platforms operating in the UK must proactively detect and remove this material rather than wait for user reports, with Ofcom able to fine non-compliant platforms up to £18 million.
items.sowhat: This doesn't touch Nancy's content directly, but it signals UK platforms will be running hotter, more proactive sexual-content detection through November — keep captions/visuals firmly on the educational, consensual, clearly-adult side of the line to avoid getting swept up in overzealous moderation.
items.caption: UK fam, heads up: from Nov 6 a few very specific categories of extreme content become flat-out illegal there, and platforms now have to hunt for it proactively, not just wait for someone to report it. We'll keep doing what we do: talking pleasure like grown-ups, zero drama. 💛

items.title: TikTok Shop Tightens 'Sexualized Behavior' Rules for Sellers and Creators
items.summary: TikTok Shop published a new 'Prohibited Content for Platform Safety' policy for US sellers and creators on August 4, 2026, explicitly barring nudity and sexualized behavior in shoppable videos and LIVEs alongside stronger minor-protection rules. The policy applies regardless of a seller's intent or target audience, so even wellness-framed content can be flagged if it reads as sexualized.
items.sowhat: Keep Nancy's TikTok Shop videos and LIVEs strictly product-education framed with zero innuendo, since the rule applies no matter what audience you're actually trying to reach.
items.caption: TikTok Shop just drew a brighter line around 'sexualized' content, intent doesn't matter, vibe does. We'll keep our LIVEs informative, playful, and policy-proof. 💡🛍️

items.title: Meta's Ad Policy Goes Claims-Based for Sexual Health
items.summary: In late July 2026 Meta rewrote its Health & Wellness advertising standards, replacing blanket category rejections with claim-by-claim review, so ads for sexual health, wellness, and reproductive products can run if each individual claim complies. Ads that are overtly sexual, pleasure-focused, or use close-up body-part imagery remain banned under the revised standard.
items.sowhat: Audit Nancy's Meta ad copy and creative line-by-line for compliant wellness framing instead of assuming the whole category is blocked, clean claims can now get approved.
items.caption: Plot twist from Meta: it's not about what you sell anymore, it's about what you say. Claims > categories now. More honest wellness talk, zero clickbait, that's our whole vibe anyway. 💬✨
